sentences.text: Antarctilamna was an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish that possessed robust spines located in front of the first dorsal fin, which lacked a deep insertion area. The fish also had distinctive diplodont teeth featuring small intermediate cusps.

Antarctilamna ultima is the first recorded Devonian cartilaginous fish known from a juvenile specimen. The juvenile status of this individual is supported by its small size and a head and branchial region exceeding a quarter of its body length.

The genus Antarctilamna was described by Young in 1982 and includes two species: Antarctilamna prisca and Antarctilamna ultima. Fossils of Antarctilamna have been discovered in Antarctica and Australia, with the most recently occurring species found at the Waterloo Farm lagerstätte in South Africa. The description of Antarctilamna prisca is based on material from both Antarctic and New South Wales localities.
Antarctilamna ultima is described from an individual approximately 1 meter long, though estimates suggest it could have reached several meters in length.
Studies suggest large sharks may have entered the Waterloo Farm estuary to forage, though it is also possible they gave birth there, using the lake as a nursery.

It is debated whether Antarctilamna is related to xenacanths or represents a basal chondrichthyan. The parent group of Antarctilamna is the family Antarctilamnidae, and the genus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Antarctilamna lived from the Lochkovian to the Famennian stages, between 419.62 and 358.86 million years ago.
